blocking: The claim "a recurrent state is inherently read_write, so uninitialized_poison cannot hold it" is false. A two-buffer ping-pong (state_a written by stage 0, state_b by stage 1) passes preflight_submission. The recorded refusal is an artefact of declaring one buffer read_write in every stage.
should_fix: test_a_partial_final_state_write_is_unsafe opened the else branch too, so it tested an out-of-bounds handoff write instead of a partial result write.
test_a_stale_handoff_slot_is_refused used STAGE-1 on an unsigned index, underflowing for STAGE=0; the real refusal was "slot 1 never written", not a stale read.
Copy-width arithmetic: 512 KiB at 4 GB/s is 129 us, not 926 us, so the single-thread copy does not explain the harness cut cost.
device_zero was never measured (blocked), yet Q.md cited it as measured.
744 GB/s vs 630 GB/s, and a wall-clock floor mixed into a GPU table.
notes: test_publishing_more_pieces refuses through "final_state never written", not through an unconsumed slot.

blocking: The retraction's replacement rationale claimed the ping-pong doubles the storage; measured totals are 262144 B = 262144 B at paper and 1024 B = 1024 B at small, so there is no storage penalty.
